purpose: Second batch of fresh routing holdout prompts (152). Together with new-heldout-prompts.json (48) they form the 200-prompt held-out set. Authored for this evaluation; not sampled from calibration tasks, Laya training data or the first 48. Written only, not measured: the calibration worker measures them in the Nov 5 pass. See dedup-heldout.json for the overlap check.

tasks.prompt: Write a Python function that converts a duration string such as '1h30m15s', '45m' or '90s' into total seconds and raises ValueError on malformed input. Add pytest cases for the edge inputs.
Write a Bash script that renames every .jpeg file in a directory to .jpg, skips any name that would collide with an existing file, and prints a one-line summary of what it renamed and skipped.
Write a JavaScript debounce helper with 'leading' and 'trailing' options and a cancel method. Include a short usage example with a search box.

Write a PostgreSQL query that returns each customer's most recent order and its total using a window function. Tables: customers(id, name) and orders(id, customer_id, placed_at, total). Customers with no orders should still appear.
Write a C# extension method that splits an IEnumerable<T> into lists of a given maximum size without enumerating the source twice, plus xUnit tests for empty, exact and uneven inputs.

Write a small Python command-line tool using argparse that takes a CSV path and a column name and prints that column's min, max and mean. Give a clear error message for a missing column or non-numeric values.
Implement an LRU cache in Java with O(1) get and put, a configurable capacity and an optional eviction listener. Explain how you would make it thread-safe and add tests that assert eviction order.

Write a Node.js script that downloads a list of URLs with at most five requests in flight, retries transient failures with exponential backoff and jitter, and writes a JSON summary of successes and failures. Use only the standard library.
Build a Go package implementing a token-bucket rate limiter keyed by string, with background cleanup of idle keys and a clock interface so the tests can run without sleeping.

Implement a Python function that merges busy intervals from several calendars given as lists of timezone-aware (start, end) datetimes. Normalise to UTC, merge overlapping and touching intervals, and return the free gaps within a given working window. Include tests.

Write a React hook, useLocalStorageState, that keeps state in sync across browser tabs through the storage event, tolerates corrupt JSON, and does not break during server-side rendering. Include a test using React Testing Library.

Write a Rust command-line tool that scans a directory tree for duplicate files by comparing sizes first and content hashes second, then prints each group of duplicates and the total bytes wasted. Avoid reading files whose size is unique.

Implement a write-ahead log for a Python key-value store: append-only records with checksums, correct fsync ordering, replay on startup that stops cleanly at the first torn record, and compaction that does not lose writes arriving during the compaction. Include crash-simulation tests.

Write a Kotlin coroutine pipeline with bounded channels and several parallel workers that still emits results in input order. It must apply backpressure, cancel cleanly on the first failure, and leak no coroutines. Include tests that prove ordering and cancellation.

Implement a consistent-hash ring with virtual nodes in TypeScript that supports weighted nodes and adding or removing a node with minimal key movement. Provide a deterministic test that measures the fraction of keys remapped when a node is removed.

Implement Raft-style leader election in Go on top of an in-memory network simulator, with randomized election timeouts, term handling and vote granting rules. Write tests for a clean election, a network partition and a split vote. Log replication is out of scope.

Write a Python library for optimistic concurrency on a REST resource: ETag generation, If-Match enforcement with 412 and 428 responses, and a pluggable merge hook for conflicting updates. Provide Flask integration tests that exercise a lost-update race.
My Python function ends with 'return data.strip' and callers print '<built-in method strip of str object ...>' instead of the text. What is wrong and what is the fix?
A loop written as 'for i in range(len(items) + 1): print(items[i])' crashes with IndexError on the last pass. Explain why and give the corrected loop, including the more idiomatic form.
git pull into a freshly cloned-then-reinitialised repository fails with 'fatal: refusing to merge unrelated histories'. What happened, and what is the safe way to proceed?
In JavaScript, [1, 10, 2, 21].sort() returns [1, 10, 2, 21] instead of ascending numbers. Why does that happen and how do I fix it?
My SQL query 'SELECT * FROM tickets WHERE closed_at = NULL' returns no rows even though many tickets are open. Explain the cause and write the right query.

A Docker container built from my image starts and immediately exits with code 0 when I run it with docker run -d. The Dockerfile ends with CMD ["bash"]. Why, and how should a long-running service be set up?
A Flask app behind nginx on HTTPS builds redirects and url_for(_external=True) links with http:// instead of https://. Diagnose the cause and fix it without hard-coding the scheme.

A pandas merge of a 1M-row orders frame with a customers frame returns 3.2M rows. I expected one row per order. Explain the likely causes, how to confirm which one applies, and how to make the merge fail loudly in future.

A Java service's heap grows steadily until OutOfMemoryError about every two days. A heap dump shows huge numbers of values retained through ThreadLocal on thread-pool threads. Explain the mechanism and how to fix it.

A cron job runs correctly when I execute the script by hand but silently does nothing from crontab. The script uses relative paths and a node binary installed through nvm. Walk through the likely causes and how to verify each.
After I added a useEffect that calls setState from an object prop listed in its dependency array, my React component re-renders forever. Explain why it loops and give two ways to fix it.

A PostgreSQL query became about 100 times slower after a major-version upgrade. EXPLAIN now shows a sequential scan where an index scan was used before, and the table was bulk-loaded during the migration. What should I check and in what order?

A test passes alone but fails intermittently on CI when the suite runs in parallel. The tests share a SQLite file path under /tmp and a module-level singleton for configuration. Lay out how to prove which shared state is responsible and how to make the suite order-independent.

A Go service shows p99 latency spikes to 800 ms every two minutes while CPU stays low and GC pauses are ruled out. A goroutine dump taken during a spike shows many goroutines blocked on one mutex that guards a metrics map also read by the scrape handler. Find the root cause and propose a fix with its tradeoffs.

After deploying a slower message handler, a Kafka consumer group rebalances every few minutes and throughput collapses, though no consumer crashes. Explain the interaction of max.poll.interval.ms, batch size and handler time, and fix it without giving up at-least-once delivery.

A counter stored in Redis occasionally moves backwards after a failover to a replica. Explain how asynchronous replication produces this, what guarantees Redis does and does not give here, and design a fix suitable for a billing-adjacent counter.

A Python asyncio service hangs under load. py-spy shows the event loop thread inside a blocking HTTP call, and some requests deadlock when a sync helper calls loop.run_until_complete from a thread-pool worker. Explain the failure chain and give a minimal, safe restructuring.
Rename the single-letter variables and magic numbers in a 40-line Python function that computes shipping cost from weight and zone, without changing behaviour. Show the before and after.
Replace a chain of nested if/else statements that map HTTP status codes to messages with a lookup table in JavaScript, keeping the default case identical.
Convert a Java class that uses string concatenation inside loops to build a report into one that uses StringBuilder, and extract the repeated formatting into a private method.
Turn a Python function with three boolean flag parameters into three small, well-named functions or an enum parameter, and update the call sites in a short example.
Remove duplicated try/except blocks around five database calls in a Python module by introducing a single context manager or decorator, with identical error behaviour.
Replace manual index loops in a Go function that filters and transforms a slice with a clearer single-pass version, and keep the original allocation behaviour in mind.

Split a 600-line Express route file that mixes validation, database access and response formatting into controller, service and repository layers. Explain the new file layout and show the migration steps so the routes keep passing their existing tests.

A C# class hierarchy uses inheritance for Report, PdfReport, CsvReport and EmailedPdfReport, causing combinatorial subclasses. Refactor to composition with a renderer and a delivery strategy, and describe how to do it in reviewable steps.
Convert a callback-heavy Node.js module that reads, transforms and writes files into async/await with proper error propagation, keeping the exported function signatures backward compatible.

Replace a global mutable configuration dictionary used throughout a Python application with an explicitly passed, immutable settings object. Describe an incremental plan that never breaks the build, and show the first two steps.
Untangle a Rust function that parses, validates and applies a configuration in one 150-line match statement into separate stages with a typed intermediate representation and better errors.

Refactor a SQL-heavy reporting module that builds queries by string formatting into parameterised queries with a small query-builder helper, eliminating injection risk while keeping the report outputs byte-identical.

A monolith's billing code reads and writes the users table directly from nine modules. Plan and demonstrate an incremental extraction behind a narrow interface that could later become a service, including how to keep data consistent during the transition and how to verify equivalence.

Refactor a TypeScript codebase from loosely typed 'any' payloads to a discriminated-union event model across producers and consumers without a flag-day change. Show how to introduce the types, narrow at the boundary and phase out the old shape safely.

Replace a hand-rolled, lock-protected in-memory cache used across a multithreaded C++ service with a design that removes the lock-ordering hazard. Explain the invariants being preserved and how to prove no behavioural regressions under concurrency.

Restructure a 2,000-line Python data-pipeline script whose steps communicate through module-level globals into testable, idempotent stages. Provide the target design, a characterisation-test strategy to capture current behaviour first, and the order of changes.

Migrate a large Django project from function-based views with ad-hoc permission checks to class-based views with a central permission policy. Cover how to find every check, avoid silently widening access, and verify authorization parity.
Review this change: a Python function opens a file with open(path) and never closes it, then returns the parsed contents. List the problems and show the corrected version.
Review a pull request that adds a JavaScript function comparing two floating-point prices with ===. Explain the risk and suggest the fix, with a one-line test.
A pull request hard-codes an API base URL and a timeout of 30 seconds directly in five Go files. Write the review comment and the suggested change.
Review a SQL migration that adds a NOT NULL column without a default to a table with millions of rows. Explain what will happen in production and how to roll it out safely.
Review a Dockerfile that runs apt-get update and apt-get install on separate RUN lines, runs as root, and copies the whole build context. List the issues in priority order.
Review a Python pull request that catches bare 'except:' around a network call and returns None on failure. Say what can go wrong and what to do instead.

Review a pull request that adds JWT authentication to an Express API: tokens signed with HS256 from an env var, no expiry check beyond library defaults, and the user id taken from the token body. Identify security and correctness gaps and rank them.

Review a Go pull request that adds a worker pool: goroutines range over a shared results slice, the error channel is unbuffered, and the pool is never shut down. Find the concurrency bugs and propose fixes.
Review a React pull request that fetches data in useEffect without cleanup, stores derived values in state, and uses array index as list keys. Explain each issue's user-visible effect and the fix.

Review a Terraform change that opens a security group to 0.0.0.0/0 on port 22 for a debugging session, adds a public S3 bucket for 'temporary' exports and removes a lifecycle prevent_destroy on a database. Say what you would block, what you would allow with changes, and why.

Review a Python pull request that adds caching to a pricing function using functools.lru_cache on a method that takes a mutable dict argument and reads the current time. Describe the bugs and a safer design.

Review a database access layer change that wraps each repository call in its own transaction and then calls three of them from one service method. Explain the consistency problems and suggest where the transaction boundary belongs.

Review a pull request that implements password reset: it emails a link with a six-digit code, stores the code in plaintext, checks it with a normal string comparison, allows unlimited attempts and keeps the code valid for 24 hours. Produce a prioritised security review and a concrete redesign.

Review a change introducing an in-process event bus with asynchronous handlers in a payments service. Handlers may run out of order, retried handlers are not idempotent, and a handler failure is only logged. Assess the correctness risks and what you would require before merging.

Review a Rust pull request wrapping a C library with unsafe FFI: raw pointers are stored in a struct that implements Send and Sync, a destructor frees memory the C side may also free, and string lengths are trusted. Identify soundness holes and give the minimal fixes.

Review a pull request that adds a multi-tenant cache keyed by request path only, with tenant resolved from a header after the cache lookup. Explain the data-leak scenario, any related cache-poisoning issues and a corrected key and flow.

Review a distributed lock implementation built on Redis SET with an expiry that releases by deleting the key without checking ownership, and whose critical section can exceed the expiry. Walk through the failure interleavings and recommend a robust alternative with its limits.
Plan a one-week task list for adding dark mode to an existing React web app with about 40 components, in order, with the main risk for each day.
Outline the steps to set up a nightly encrypted backup of a Postgres database to object storage, including how to verify restores. Keep it to a short checklist.
I need to add pagination to a REST endpoint that currently returns all rows. List the decisions to make and the order to implement and release the change.
Make a checklist for onboarding a new developer to a Python service repo on their first day, including accounts, local setup and a first small change.
Plan how to rotate an API key used by three services with no downtime. Give the steps in order and what to monitor.
Break 'add CSV export to the reports page' into small tasks with rough sizes and note which can run in parallel.

Plan the migration of a Rails app's background jobs from a database-backed queue to Redis-based Sidekiq with zero lost jobs. Include a rollout sequence, dual-running period, monitoring and a rollback.

We want to move from a single Postgres instance to one primary with two read replicas. Plan the application changes, the consistency issues for read-your-writes, the rollout stages and the failure drills.

Create a plan to introduce end-to-end tests for a checkout flow in a web store that currently has none. Cover scope, test data, flakiness control, CI integration and how to measure whether it is paying off.
Plan a staged rollout of a new pricing calculation behind a feature flag, including shadow computation, comparison metrics, thresholds for proceeding and the rollback trigger.

Design a six-week plan for a team of three to replace a legacy SOAP integration with a REST client, keeping both working until partners have moved. Identify the milestones and the largest uncertainty.
Plan how to reduce a mobile app's cold-start time from 4 seconds to under 2. Describe how to profile, what to try first, how to guard against regressions and how to report progress.

Plan a zero-downtime migration of a 2 TB MySQL database to a new schema with a changed primary-key type, while the application keeps writing. Cover backfill, dual writes, verification, cutover, rollback and the point of no return.

Propose an architecture and delivery plan for multi-region active-active deployment of a user-session service, including conflict resolution, data residency constraints, failure modes, testing strategy and phased rollout.

A company wants to split a 12-year-old Java monolith into services within a year with a team of eight while shipping features. Produce a strategy: how to choose seams, sequence extractions, keep delivery going, handle data ownership and decide when to stop.

Plan the response and the engineering follow-up to a leaked-credentials incident where a cloud access key was exposed in a public repository for 36 hours. Cover immediate containment, investigation, customer communication decisions and long-term controls.

Design a plan to introduce schema-validated event contracts across 30 services owned by six teams, including governance, compatibility rules, tooling, migration order and how to resolve disagreements about ownership.
What is the difference between a process and a thread, and when would I choose multiprocessing over threading in Python? Keep the answer short with one example.
Explain what a database index does, why it can slow writes, and when an index will not be used by a query planner.
Summarise the difference between REST and GraphQL for a small team building a mobile app backend, and give a one-line recommendation.
What does semantic versioning promise, and where do people commonly misunderstand it when upgrading dependencies?
Explain how HTTPS certificate validation works from the browser's point of view, in plain language and in about ten sentences.
Briefly compare SQLite, PostgreSQL and MongoDB for storing user-generated documents in a hobby project, and pick one.
Compare Kubernetes, Nomad and plain systemd units for running eight small services on three servers. Address operations burden, failure handling, networking and when each stops being appropriate.
Evaluate the main approaches to feature flags: config files, a database table and a hosted service. Cover latency, consistency across instances, audit trail, cleanup of stale flags and cost.
Explain the practical differences between OAuth 2.0 authorization code with PKCE, client credentials and device flow, and which one fits a CLI tool, a backend job and a smart TV app.
Compare row-level locking, optimistic versioning and serializable isolation for preventing double-booking in a reservation system. Discuss throughput, retry behaviour and failure modes.

Survey strategies for storing and querying time-series metrics at moderate scale: Postgres with partitioning, a dedicated TSDB and columnar files. Give selection criteria and a recommendation for 50k points per second.

What are the tradeoffs between monorepos and polyrepos for twelve services shared by four teams? Cover build times, ownership, dependency updates and tooling cost, and say what would change your answer.
Explain how modern CPUs' memory ordering affects lock-free code, using x86 and ARM as examples, and what a programmer must do in C++ or Rust to stay correct on both.

Analyse CRDTs versus operational transformation for a collaborative text editor with offline editing. Cover convergence guarantees, metadata growth, garbage collection, intent preservation, and what each demands of the server.

Assess the security and operational tradeoffs of using a service mesh for mutual TLS between 100 services versus application-level mTLS libraries. Include certificate lifecycle, performance, debugging, blast radius and organisational fit.

Explain how the CAP theorem and PACELC apply to choosing a datastore for a global shopping cart. Distinguish what is a theorem from what is a design heuristic, and recommend a design with explicit consistency choices.

Compare approaches to differential privacy for releasing aggregate usage statistics from an app: local versus central models, noise mechanisms and privacy budget accounting. Say what utility loss to expect at 100k users and where practice usually goes wrong.
Write a two-sentence commit message and a short pull request description for a change that fixes an off-by-one error in page numbering on the invoices list.
Draft a friendly Slack message asking a teammate to review a small pull request today, mentioning that it touches the login page and is about 80 lines.
Write a README opening section (title, one-paragraph summary and install command) for a Python command-line tool that converts Markdown files to PDF.
Write a concise error message for a CLI when the user passes a config file that does not exist, including what was tried and what to do next.
Rewrite this sentence to be clear and neutral for release notes: 'We finally fixed the awful bug where exports were totally broken for big accounts.'
Write a polite email to a customer explaining that their requested feature is not on the roadmap this year, but offering a workaround and a way to follow future updates.

Write a postmortem summary for an incident in which a certificate expired and took down an internal API for 47 minutes. Include timeline, impact, root cause, what went well, what did not and action items with owners as placeholders.

Write the migration guide section for a library's v2 release that renames three functions, changes a default timeout and removes Python 3.8 support. Include before and after code examples and a compatibility shim.
Draft an architecture decision record choosing PostgreSQL over DynamoDB for a new order service. Include context, options considered, decision, consequences and what would trigger revisiting it.
Write an onboarding doc for on-call engineers covering how paging works, the first ten minutes of an incident, severity definitions and when to escalate. Aim for a skimmable one-page layout.
Write a clear public changelog entry and a separate internal note for a release that quietly changes how rounding works in invoice totals. The public text must be honest without causing alarm.
Write API reference documentation for a POST /v1/webhooks endpoint, covering request fields, validation errors, idempotency, signature verification and a worked example in curl.

Write a design proposal summary of about 400 words arguing for adopting TypeScript in a 60,000-line JavaScript codebase. Address cost, rollout, risks and measurable benefits, written for sceptical senior engineers.

Write a threat-model document introduction and executive summary for a new file-sharing feature that lets users create expiring public links. It must be useful to both engineers and a non-technical product lead, and name the top five threats with mitigations.

Draft a candid but constructive engineering blog post explaining why a team reversed a migration to microservices after eighteen months. Keep it specific, avoid blame, and make the lessons transferable.

Write a customer-facing incident communication sequence for a data-corruption bug that affected 0.3 percent of accounts: initial notice, mid-incident update and final summary. Balance transparency, legal caution and clarity.

Write the RFC for introducing a deprecation policy across a public API: principles, timelines, communication channels, exceptions for security fixes and how breaking changes are versioned. Anticipate and address three likely objections.
Given a long meeting transcript, list every decision made and the person who owns each action item, with the timestamp where it was agreed.
Read a 30-page API reference and answer: which endpoints accept pagination, and what are the parameter names for each? Quote the section headings you used.
Scan a large application log and report how many distinct error messages appear, with the three most frequent and the first time each occurred.
From a long product requirements document, extract all mentions of performance targets with their numbers and units, and note the section each came from.
Summarise a 40-page onboarding handbook into a one-page cheat sheet for new hires, keeping the section order.
Read a long email thread about a vendor contract and state, in five bullets, where the parties currently disagree.
Compare two versions of a 60-page terms-of-service document and list every substantive change in data retention, liability and termination, separating wording tweaks from real differences.
Given a long codebase export of a billing module (about 40 files), explain how a refund flows from API call to ledger entry and list every place that can reject it.
Read three quarters of support-ticket exports and identify recurring complaint themes, how they moved over time, and which are linked to specific releases mentioned in the release notes.
Given a long design document and the code that was eventually written, find where the implementation diverges from the design and rate each divergence by risk.
From a big configuration repository with many environment overlays, determine which settings differ between staging and production and flag any that look unintended.
Review a long research paper and its appendix and report which claims in the abstract are supported by tables, which rely on assumptions stated only in the appendix, and which are not supported.

Reconcile a long chronological incident chat export with the monitoring graphs described in the attached notes and build a single corrected timeline, marking where the chat's claims contradict the data.

Given an entire legacy codebase's documentation, tickets and commit messages, reconstruct the undocumented business rules for tax calculation, cite the evidence for each rule and flag rules that conflict across sources.

Analyse a very long set of distributed traces and service logs to find why a rare checkout timeout occurs, ruling out at least three plausible but wrong explanations with evidence, and state remaining uncertainty.

Audit a large contract bundle (master agreement, five amendments and several order forms) for the effective payment terms, renewal conditions and liability caps after all amendments, citing clause numbers and showing which text supersedes which.

Read a multi-hundred-page security assessment and the engineering team's responses, then produce a prioritised remediation list that merges duplicate findings, challenges any response that does not actually address the finding, and records open questions.
Find every file in the repository that defines a function named parse_config and list the file paths with line numbers.
Run the project's test suite and report which tests fail, with the first line of each failure message.
Check which version of the 'requests' library the project pins in its dependency files and whether any file pins a different version.
Look at the last ten commits on the current branch and summarise what each changed in one line.
Count how many TODO and FIXME comments exist in the source tree, grouped by directory.
Find out why the build fails on a clean checkout: run the build, read the error, locate the offending configuration and propose a fix, citing the file and line.
Use repository search to find all callers of a deprecated function across the codebase, group them by module, and produce a migration checklist ordered by risk.
Inspect the Dockerfile and docker-compose file, run the container build and tell me why the image is larger than 1 GB, then list the three largest layers and how to shrink them.
Check the project for hard-coded secrets using search and git history, report anything suspicious with file and commit references, and do not print the secret values themselves.
Find the slowest five tests by running the suite with timing output, then read the slowest one and suggest one concrete way to speed it up.
Compare the environment variables read in the code with those listed in the deployment manifests and report any that are read but never set, or set but never read.
Use git blame and log to find which commit introduced a regression in the date-formatting function, and show the diff hunk responsible.

Bisect a regression: the integration suite passed two weeks ago and fails now. Use git bisect with an automated test command, find the first bad commit, explain the cause and propose a minimal fix with a regression test.

Investigate a memory leak in a long-running Node service using the available tooling: reproduce it with a load script, capture heap snapshots at two points, identify the retaining path and verify the fix by repeating the measurement.

Audit the repository's dependency tree for known-vulnerable or abandoned packages using the package manager's tools, determine which are actually reachable from the application code, and produce a prioritised upgrade plan that notes breaking changes.

Reproduce a flaky test: run it in a loop under varying load until it fails, capture logs from a failing and a passing run, diff the sequences, identify the race or ordering assumption, and show a fix that passes a thousand consecutive runs.
